Android 16 and later only hand a scanned tag to apps you\'ve allowed. Until OpenTasker is allowed, scanning a tag does nothing and NFC profiles never run.

Lets health contexts read steps, heart rate, sleep and exercise from Health Connect. The readings are checked on a schedule while OpenTasker is in the background, so background reading has to be allowed too. OpenTasker only reads, and never writes health data.
Health Connect isn\'t on this phone. Android 14 and later have it built in, and on Android 9 to 13 it\'s an app from Google. It doesn\'t run on Android 8.
Health Connect needs an update before OpenTasker can read it in the background.
Health Connect is part of Android here and updates with Google Play system updates. Install the latest one so OpenTasker can read it in the background.
Health Connect didn\'t allow every reading. Tap the row again to open its settings.
Health Connect isn\'t letting OpenTasker read %1$s in the background, so this context can\'t match. Allow it in Setup under Read Health Connect.
Health Connect is missing, needs an update, or can\'t be read in the background on this phone, so this context can\'t match. Setup under Read Health Connect says which.
Reading %1$s from Health Connect failed twice in a row, so this context can\'t match until a read works. The app log has the error.

OpenTasker reads Health Connect only for profiles you set up with a health context, like steps today or your latest heart rate.

It can read steps, heart rate, sleep and exercise, and only the ones your profiles use. Readings are checked on the shortest schedule any of your health contexts asks for, at most every 15 minutes. That happens in the background, so a profile can run while OpenTasker isn't open.

OpenTasker never writes to Health Connect and doesn't send your readings anywhere. You can take the access back at any time in Health Connect.

Needed for scene overlays and controls displayed over other apps, and for a trigger to open an app, a link or the home screen while OpenTasker is in the background. Android calls this Display over other apps.
Scenes, overlay UI, opening apps and links from a trigger
Something is already running. Wait for it to finish.
Lets a task lock the screen. This is the only thing OpenTasker asks for here.

Android only lets an app lock the screen if you make it a device admin. OpenTasker asks for one permission in that role, force-lock, and for nothing else. It cannot wipe your device, set a password policy, or read anything. One catch worth knowing before you turn it on: Android will not let you uninstall OpenTasker until you turn this back off, and you can do that here.
OpenTasker uses this to lock the screen when a task asks it to. It requests no other admin permission.

Lets Write Setting change the Global and Secure tables. Android has no screen for this and no app can ask for it, so you grant it once from a computer with the phone plugged in and USB debugging on. Run:

%1$s

It survives reboots but not an uninstall. On Xiaomi and other MIUI builds you also need "USB debugging (Security settings)" turned on, which is a second switch next to the usual one.

This does not cover airplane mode. Writing that setting only moves a flag: the radios stay on unless the system receives a broadcast no ordinary app is allowed to send, so airplane mode still needs Shizuku.

Needed for Location contexts and for reading Wi-Fi network names. Choose Precise when Android asks. Approximate location blurs your position too much for small geofences, and Android won\'t show Wi-Fi names with it.
Only approximate location is allowed right now. Wi-Fi network names and small geofences need precise location, so tap Request and choose Precise.

Users can decline and keep using foreground-only automations. Public reliability still needs device verification.

These run as the Android shell user, with the same reach as adb. Keep the script where that user can read it, like /data/local/tmp or shared storage, and enter the SHA-256 from a trusted copy (sha256sum prints it). OpenTasker reads the file, checks the hash and runs exactly what it checked, so an edited script refuses to run until you approve it again.
